item.title: COP31 talks face early friction over future of fossil fuels
item.description:
ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 13 (Reuters) - Big fossil fuel producers and consumers at the COP31 climate talks are resisting any deal that would specify firm new targets or a shift away from oil, gas and coal, observers said on Friday as the first week of talks drew to a close.

That poses a challenge for summit host Turkey and lead negotiator Australia, which has another week to land the kind of ambitious agreement climate advocates say is needed to address the worsening impacts of global warming.

item.title: Palestinian teen reunites with family after month in Israeli jail
item.description:
Looking tiny in his adult-size grey prison jumpsuit, 15-year-old Palestinian Ezzedine al-Lahalia appeared stunned as his mother embraced him after a month in an Israeli jail. 

His first request was a child's wish for his favourite food: stuffed cabbage and shawarma.

The teenager, who had been charged with throwing stones, was reunited with his family Thursday night in an emotional scene witnessed by an AFP photographer.

item.title: Gore blasts 'insane' Saudi veto power at climate talks
item.description:
Former US vice president Al Gore said it was "literally insane" that oil-producing nations such as Saudi Arabia could block global action against climate change, calling for sweeping reforms to UN negotiations.

Speaking to AFP on the sidelines of the COP31 summit in Antalya, Turkey, Gore said UN climate talks needed to replace the consensus-based decision-making system with a supermajority model.

item.title: France favours adding pressure on Yemen's Houthis, foreign ministry spokesperson says
item.description:
PARIS, Nov 13 (Reuters) - It is necessary to raise pressure on Yemen's Houthis so that they end their attacks in the region, notably on Saudi Arabia, France's foreign ministry spokesperson said on Friday.

"Our position is that it is necessary to increase pressure on the Houthis so that they put an end to their unacceptable attacks and provocations, particularly against Saudi territory, but not only there," Pascal Confavreux told a news conference.

item.title: At least nine detained protesting at blast-hit Turkey steel plant
item.description:
Turkey's security forces on Friday detained at least nine people protesting a ban on bringing mobile phones into a steel plant hit by a deadly explosion this week, a workers' collective said.

Workers arriving for their morning shift at the HABAS steel factory were told to leave their mobile phones at a security checkpoint, said a spokesman for the Aegean Workers' Collective.

Instead, some of them gathered at the facility's entrance to protest.

item.title: Germany's Merz asks Trump for 'no surprises' from Putin talks
item.description:
BERLIN, Nov 13 (Reuters) - German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Friday urged US President Donald Trump not to spring any surprises during expected talks on Ukraine with Russian President Vladimir Putin in China next week.

"Some here in Dublin fear this could turn into a 'second Anchorage moment'," said Merz, referring to the Trump-Putin summit in Anchorage, Alaska, that European leaders had viewed as a potentially pivotal moment in efforts to end the war in Ukraine.

item.title: Belgian ministers at odds over Iran's alleged role in refrigerator cyberattacks
item.description:
BRUSSELS, Nov 13 (Reuters) - Belgian Interior Minister Bernard Quintin said Iran was "very likely" behind the recent refrigerator cyberattacks on European shops, while Foreign Minister Maxime Prévot said there was insufficient evidence to draw conclusions.

"There was enough evidence from our security services for me to say that Iran is very likely behind the cyberattacks we have seen targeting our shops," Quintin told Belgian broadcaster VRT NWS Thursday evening.

Quintin made similar comments earlier on Thursday, but Prévot struck a more cautious tone.

item.title: Respiratory illnesses rise in Gaza with worst to come as winter floods arrive, WHO says
item.description:
By Olivia Le Poidevin

GENEVA, Nov 13 (Reuters) - The World Health Organization warned on Friday of surging respiratory illnesses in Gaza, with worse expected after heavy rains flooded tens of thousands of tents housing displaced Palestinians.

“The numbers already show the pressure. Acute respiratory infections are 33,000 cases higher than at the same time last year,” DrReinhilde Van De Weerdt, WHO Representative in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, told reporters in Geneva from Jerusalem.

item.title: France criticises 'demagogic' move by Israel to ban hard-left leader Melenchon
item.description:
PARIS, Nov 13 (Reuters) - France has criticised as "demagogic" a decision by Israel to ban French hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchonand another leading figure in his France Unbowed (La France Insoumise) party from entering the country.

Israel's Foreign Ministry said on Thursday it would bar Melenchon and Mathilde Panot, the party’s parliamentary group chair, over "the extreme anti-Israel stance of La France Insoumise party and the outrageous statements made by its leaders."

item.title: Six-year-old Gaza burn victim caught in Israeli dispute over aid
item.description:
By Nidal al-Mughrabi and Dawoud Abu Alkas

CAIRO/GAZA, Nov 13 (Reuters) - The excruciating burns run around the side of Masa Yassin's tiny face, behind her ear, over her scalp and down her neck.

Since her family's tent burst into flames when a nearby cooking gas tank exploded in July, part of the 6-year-old girl's treatment has been a clear plastic 3D-printed mask, which helps manage swelling and control the scars on her face.

item.title: IAEA increasingly concerned about Iranian enrichment plant, its report says
item.description:
VIENNA, Nov 13 (Reuters) - The UN nuclear watchdog is "increasingly concerned" about a uranium-enrichment plant at Isfahan that Iran declared to it last year but has still not let the watchdog inspect, it said in a confidential report on Iran on Friday seen by Reuters.

Iran has not let International Atomic Energy Agency inspectors return to any of its nuclear facilities bombed by Israel and the United States in a 12-day campaign in June last year that destroyed or badly damaged Iran's other uranium enrichment plants, the heart of its nuclear programme.

item.title: US denies Iran's claim that it attacked early-warning radar in Bahrain
item.description:
Nov 13 (Reuters) - The US military denied Iran's claim on Friday to have attacked a US early-warning radar in Bahrain, saying its forces had shot down two one-way attack drones launched by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps toward Bahrain with no harm caused.

Iran had said its strike was in retaliation for what it described as an air attack on a telecommunications tower in its Hormozgan province, according to Iranian state media.
